about.title: Care and diagnostics, without the runaround
body: Aaradhana Clinic and Labs was started to solve a problem every family in Goparasanallur and Poonamallee knows well — getting a diagnosis usually means two trips: one to see a doctor, another to a separate lab for blood work, then a wait for reports before anyone can actually treat you.

Led by Dr. Venmathi S, our clinic combines a general physician's consultation room with an in-house diagnostic lab, so common tests can be drawn the same visit and reviewed against your symptoms without losing days in between. Whether it's a fever that won't settle, routine diabetes and blood pressure monitoring, or a full-body health checkup, we try to get you an answer — not just an appointment.

blogPosts.title: Why an Annual Health Checkup Catches Problems Before They Become Emergencies
blogPosts.excerpt: Most chronic conditions show warning signs in routine blood work years before symptoms appear. Here's what a basic annual checkup actually looks for.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Venmathi S
content: By the time diabetes or high blood pressure start causing noticeable symptoms, they've often been quietly present for years. A basic annual checkup — blood sugar, blood pressure, lipid profile and a physical exam — is designed to catch exactly this window, while it's still easy to manage.

One reason people skip checkups is the hassle: a consultation here, a lab visit there, then a wait for results before anyone tells you what they mean. That gap is exactly why we built Aaradhana Clinic and Labs around doing both in one place — so the barrier to getting checked is as low as possible.

A good checkup isn't just a stack of numbers. What matters is whether someone looks at your results against your age, family history and lifestyle, and tells you plainly what — if anything — needs attention.
If it's been more than a year since your last full checkup, that alone is a reasonable enough reason to book one. You don't need to be feeling unwell to benefit from catching something early.
